note.note:
Action Plan:
1. Urgent referral sent to local Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA) / mini-stroke clinic for assessment within the next 24–48 h (target before the weekend).  
2. Patient advised to telephone the TIA clinic/PALS in 1–2 h or tomorrow morning to confirm booking and appointment time; contact numbers provided in the consultation notes.  
3. Safety-netting: If neurological symptoms recur and are prolonged or worsen, the patient will attend the emergency department immediately; otherwise he should phone the practice for further advice.  
4. Patient encouraged to keep a symptom diary (onset, duration, pattern) to assist the specialist team.  
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• 32-year-old male (John Smith) presents with 1.5–2 months of recurrent right-sided neurological episodes.  
• Episodes:  
  – Initial frequency once per week → now several per day.  
  – Each episode lasts “a few days” then fully resolves.  
  – Symptoms during episodes: pins-and-needles in right hand, subjective weakness of right arm and right leg, colleague-noted abnormal gait, difficulty holding coffee cup, transient “something in throat” sensation (no overt dysphagia), fatigue, intermittent nausea.  
  – No speech or visual disturbance reported.  
  – Currently asymptomatic.  
• Past medical history: none significant.  
• Medications: Aspirin 75 mg daily (self-initiated; dose/route/frequency otherwise not documented).  
• Allergies: Penicillin.  
• Family history: Father underwent carotid endarterectomy for stroke prevention.  
• Social: Plastic-surgery doctor, lives with wife, non-smoker. No alcohol or drug history recorded.

Objective:
• Remote video/telephone consultation; video lost part-way.  
• No acute distress; fluent speech; no focal neurological deficit observed during call.  
• No vitals or physical examination possible.  
• No investigations available to date.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Recurrent right-sided neurological episodes  
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA) / mini-stroke.  
   - Differential diagnosis (consistent with DDx):  
     • Multiple Sclerosis (High) – episodic sensory & motor deficits lasting days.  
     • Recurrent embolic TIAs (Medium) – unilateral, complete resolution; family history.  
     • Hemiplegic/complex migraine (Low–Medium).  
     • Cervical spinal cord/nerve-root compression (Low).  
   - Investigations planned: TIA clinic to arrange carotid Doppler ultrasound, brain imaging (CT/MRI), cardiac/vascular work-up, blood tests as per protocol.  
   - Treatment planned: Continue current aspirin 75 mg daily pending specialist review; no new medications initiated today.  
   - Relevant referrals: Urgent TIA/ministroke clinic (referral sent electronically).

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected: vitals, full neurological examination, complete medication and alcohol history, vaccination status.  
● Internal conflicts: Episode duration reported as 3–4 days (exceeds classic TIA <24 h) vs working diagnosis of TIA – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Occasional audio/video dropouts but overall history understandable.
